[LUNI.3.1.1] **`_` is optional on a decimal prefix, and that holds for every
unit.** Every unit accepts the separator and none requires it: `5_s` and `5s` are the same literal, as
are `100_km` / `100km`, `23_°C` / `23°C`, `100_Ω` / `100Ω`, `45_deg` /
`45deg` — and `45°` / `45_°`, `30′` / `30_′`,
`45″` / `45_″`.

⚠ **The numeric prefix is decimal.** Hex, binary and octal prefixes are not
unit-literal prefixes at all ([LUNI.3.1.8]) — they are ambiguous with the
integer literals they are built from. So the separator is optional
universally, with no exception on either the unit or the base.

SI decides the **canonical** spelling of a quantity, and it is carried by
what the toolchain renders, not by what it refuses ([LUNI.3.1.6]).

One apparent exception is not one: `50%` is a syntax error, because a
bare `%` is the modulo operator rather than a unit symbol
([LUNI.3.1.3]). That is an operator collision, not a spacing rule.
